Active Builder V3 adoption is explicitly split to a later release-budgeted wave.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The repository needs one canonical Publish Readiness Core that composes existing readiness authorities without becoming a second quality system. The combined Core + active Builder V3 adoption exceeded the Release Risk Budget at 7/5 points across 4/3 subsystems, so this wave is intentionally split: this transaction proves the Core only. Missing authority evidence must remain UNKNOWN, pixel drift must remain non-causal, and no publishing or Page Schema mutation is allowed.
observableOutcomes: One canonical Publish Readiness contract emits deterministic PASS/BLOCK/UNKNOWN findings and an aggregate decision without becoming a second domain authority.
Every finding carries authority/source, severity, explainable reason, repairability and page/viewport/node/path localization wherever the source authority exposes it.
Current-page Fidelity accessibility/layout/performance evidence is consumed rather than reimplemented.
Responsive inheritance diagnostics are consumed read-only and remain localized to node/viewport/dimension.
Visual Diff manifest intelligence is consumed with its exact-head provenance and structured-vs-unlocalized causality boundary intact.
Canonical page inventory, template route integrity and showroom/page-route completeness evidence fail closed when absent or incomplete.
Media and commerce readiness consume existing Template Factory/Storefront evidence instead of inventing new business truth.
The Publish Readiness contract never invokes publish actions and never mutates Builder Page Schema.
The Core is independently executable and reusable, while active Builder V3 adoption remains explicitly pending and prevents full VX-PUBLISH-READINESS promotion.
unresolvedRisks: A missing template-level evidence source could be mislabeled as clean because current-page Fidelity is green.
Warnings from non-blocking authorities could accidentally become blockers or, inversely, errors could be downgraded to advisory status.
Pixel-only visual drift could be converted into a causal diagnosis or repair suggestion.
Page inventory can contain all 14 page types while some belong to another template/version or lack a draft revision.
Current-page link checks validate URL shape but cannot prove canonical shopper-route reachability without route-integrity evidence.
Commerce capability presence in binding context could be mistaken for executable commerce readiness.
Media alt checks alone could be mistaken for media production readiness while planned/internal-reference assets remain unresolved.
A PASS aggregate could be emitted when any required category is UNKNOWN.
A later UI-adoption wave must not reintroduce a parallel checklist or overclaim full capability before active V3 consumption is proven.

in: Pure deterministic Publish Readiness decision contract over existing Builder/Fidelity/Inheritance/Visual Diff/Template Factory evidence.
PASS/BLOCK/UNKNOWN semantics with UNKNOWN fail-closed at aggregate level.
Finding provenance, source authority, severity, localization, explanation and repairability metadata.
Canonical nine-category coverage: responsive/inheritance, visual drift, accessibility, media, links, commerce, required content, performance, page/route completeness.
Adversarial tests for missing/stale/mixed evidence, error/warning precedence, visual causality boundary and deterministic output.
Maturity promotion only after active UI adoption and executable proof.
Release-split boundary: Core contract and adversarial proof only; active V3 presentation adoption is deferred.
out: Publishing or changing publish persistence/action authority.
Page Schema mutation or repair operations.
Smart Intent or natural-language intent parsing.
Smart Auto-Fix or automatic mutation generation.
New screenshot capture, golden comparison or visual baseline authority.
Changing Fidelity, Visual Diff, responsive inheritance, route-integrity or Template Factory source authorities to make readiness pass.
Control Plane, guard, policy or Known Failure changes without a newly proven deficiency.
Active StorefrontVisualBuilderV3 adoption in this release transaction.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Publish readiness is a release-adjacent decision surface that composes heterogeneous authorities and can create false confidence if evidence is missing, stale or over-interpreted. The highest practically justified level is a pure fail-closed evidence aggregator with explicit authority provenance, finite state semantics, dependency closure, adversarial evidence injection and active-UI adoption proof. Formal verification of browser/application behavior is not justified because the underlying evidence producers remain executable runtime authorities.

acceptanceCriteria: The readiness aggregate can only be PASS when every required category is proven and no blocking finding exists; any required missing/unverifiable evidence yields UNKNOWN.
Fidelity diagnostics retain original codes, severity, node/component identity and viewport where available.
Responsive inheritance findings consume existing inspection output and do not call propagation/apply APIs.
Visual Diff findings preserve exact-head/template/version provenance, page/viewport localization, evidence class and repairability; pixel-only drift remains manual-review with no structured cause.
Accessibility, media, links, commerce, required-content, performance and page/route completeness are represented as distinct categories with named source authorities.
Canonical page completeness validates all 14 page types exactly once for the active template identity and cannot treat foreign/stale page rows as satisfying coverage.
Template-level evidence that is unavailable in the Builder runtime remains explicit UNKNOWN rather than being inferred from local page state.
No readiness module imports publish actions, persistence mutations, Builder mutation application or screenshot/golden capture code.
Equivalent normalized evidence produces deep-equal readiness output regardless of finding input order.
Release Risk Budget remains within policy for the wave or the UI adoption is split before implementation proceeds.
This Core-only wave must leave VX-PUBLISH-READINESS non-PROVEN because active Builder V3 adoption is intentionally deferred by Release Risk Budget.
invariants: Readiness composes evidence; it does not own the underlying accessibility, responsive, visual, route, commerce, media, content or performance truth.
UNKNOWN is never equivalent to PASS.
BLOCK dominates UNKNOWN; UNKNOWN dominates PASS at aggregate level.
A warning may remain non-blocking only when its source authority classifies it as non-error and its evidence is present.
Pixel evidence alone cannot claim a causal Page Schema defect or repair operation.
Readiness does not publish, save, mutate, persist, capture screenshots or promote golden baselines.
Template/page/source identity must be preserved across every template-level evidence input.
Core proof does not imply active UI adoption or full Publish Readiness capability completion.

failureModes: Current page has no Fidelity errors, but visual exact-head evidence is absent and readiness reports PASS.
One visual pixel hotspot is labeled as an overflow repair without structured Runtime evidence.
Fourteen stored page rows exist but one page belongs to a different template version and completeness still passes.
A hard performance issue appears as a warning because the UI maps only presentation status labels.
A safe-looking href passes syntax validation while route-integrity evidence is missing and link readiness still passes.
Media has valid alt text but Template Factory media evidence reports planned assets; readiness incorrectly passes media.
Commerce components render but engine/showroom proof is unavailable; readiness incorrectly passes commerce.
A new unknown evidence state is dropped by aggregation and produces a false clean summary.
A blocking category and an unknown category coexist but aggregate precedence incorrectly returns UNKNOWN instead of BLOCK.
Core-only proof is incorrectly used to promote the full VX-PUBLISH-READINESS capability before V3 adoption.
edgeCases: No draft revision while all document diagnostics are otherwise clean.
Fidelity warning-only accessibility issues with no errors.
Visual evidence has bounded nonzero mismatch but remains within accepted thresholds.
Visual manifest is valid but contains an unclassified warning.
Inheritance has redundant override warnings on multiple viewports.
Page inventory contains duplicate page types or unknown page types.
Template-level evidence is supplied for the correct template key but wrong version.
A current page has no image nodes while template-level media evidence is unavailable.
Route-integrity issue localizes only to config path/href rather than nodeId.
Input evidence collections arrive in different order.

specialistReviews.finding: Existing Fidelity, inheritance, visual-diff, route/showroom and Template Factory engines already own the relevant evidence; readiness should only normalize their decisions.
specialistReviews.resolution: Implement a pure adapter/aggregator with explicit source authority identifiers and no source-authority rewrites.

specialistReviews.finding: The active Builder does not currently possess all exact-head/template-level evidence, so a local clean document cannot prove template readiness.
specialistReviews.resolution: Required but unavailable evidence is represented as UNKNOWN and prevents aggregate PASS; no fallback inference is permitted.

specialistReviews.finding: Measured combined Core + active Admin UI change is 7/5 points across 4/3 subsystems.
specialistReviews.resolution: Split now: prove the Core on #701 within the existing 5/5 cumulative budget; preserve the V3 adoption patch separately and do not promote the full capability until that wave passes.

specialistReviews.finding: UI adoption is required for the full capability but is outside this release transaction after the measured risk overflow.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep UI semantics specified and preserved in the WIP branch; this Core wave proves only the reusable decision contract.

challenge.scenario: All current-page Fidelity checks pass but visual evidence is absent.
challenge.finding: Local diagnostics cannot prove exact-head visual readiness.
challenge.resolution: Visual category is UNKNOWN and aggregate is UNKNOWN.

challenge.scenario: Pixel diff fails with no structured runtime issue.
challenge.resolution: BLOCK visual drift with manual-review repairability and no causal repair.

challenge.scenario: A canonical page type is missing or duplicated in page inventory.
challenge.resolution: BLOCK page/route completeness with explicit page-type evidence.

challenge.scenario: All 14 page types exist but one has foreign template/version identity.
challenge.finding: Cardinality alone can hide mixed presentation authority.
challenge.resolution: Foreign identity cannot satisfy completeness and produces BLOCK.

challenge.scenario: Link syntax is valid but template route-integrity evidence is absent.
challenge.finding: Safe URL syntax is weaker than reachable canonical route proof.
challenge.resolution: Links retain local evidence but route reachability remains UNKNOWN; aggregate cannot PASS.

challenge.scenario: Image alt diagnostics are clean while media planning reports unresolved planned/internal-reference assets.
challenge.finding: Accessibility media checks are not production media readiness.
challenge.resolution: Media category consumes explicit media authority; unresolved states BLOCK/UNKNOWN according to source evidence.

challenge.scenario: Commerce components are present but executable engine/showroom evidence is absent.
challenge.finding: Presentation presence is not commerce readiness.
challenge.resolution: Commerce category remains UNKNOWN until canonical commerce/showroom evidence is supplied.

challenge.scenario: A BLOCK finding and UNKNOWN finding coexist.
challenge.finding: Unknown must not mask a known blocker.
challenge.resolution: Aggregate precedence is BLOCK > UNKNOWN > PASS.

challenge.scenario: Evidence lists arrive in different order.
challenge.finding: UI and truth status must not depend on enumeration order.

challenge.scenario: The Core passes all adversarial proofs while active V3 still uses its old local checklist.
challenge.finding: Core correctness is not equivalent to user-visible adoption.
challenge.resolution: Keep full VX-PUBLISH-READINESS non-PROVEN and require a separate V3-adoption wave.

proofPlan: Plan Before Code projected-scope proof and exact release-risk projection before implementation.
Core adversarial state-machine proof for PASS/BLOCK/UNKNOWN precedence and required-category completeness.
Authority mapping proof that each canonical readiness category names and preserves its existing source contract.
Localization proof for page/viewport/node/component/path/href fields when available.
Visual causality proof: pixel-only drift remains manual-review and cannot become a structured repair.
Page inventory adversarial proof for missing, duplicate, foreign-template and foreign-version rows.
Missing-evidence proof for visual, route, media and commerce categories: UNKNOWN never PASS.
Determinism/immutability proof across reordered equivalent evidence.
Source-code boundary proof forbidding publish/persistence/Builder mutation/screenshot capture imports from readiness Core.
Incremental Known Failure replay, targeted quality tests, full quality tests, TypeScript, production build, exact-head Template Factory Quality Gate v2, Completion Truth and lifecycle closure.
Capability-separation proof: Core success must not promote full VX-PUBLISH-READINESS, Smart Intent, Smart Auto-Fix or Template #3.
After Core lifecycle closure, resume the preserved V3-adoption change only in a separate release-budgeted transaction.

requirements.requirement: Canonical Publish Readiness aggregates all required evidence categories with authority provenance and fail-closed PASS/BLOCK/UNKNOWN semantics; UNKNOWN can never satisfy readiness.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Missing, stale, partial or foreign authority evidence cannot be converted to PASS.

requirements.requirement: Publish Readiness remains a read-only evidence decision contract: it does not publish, mutate Page Schema, duplicate source authorities or infer repairs from pixel evidence.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Readiness cannot become a second visual/route/commerce/media authority or invoke publish/mutation paths.

requirements.requirement: Publish Readiness Core completion does not promote the full VX-PUBLISH-READINESS capability, Smart Intent, Smart Auto-Fix or authorize Template #3; active V3 adoption remains a required separate wave.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Core-only proof cannot be reported as full Publish Readiness capability completion before active V3 adoption.

notes: Tenth Brabus hardening is release-split by measured gate evidence. Combined Core + active V3 adoption produced Release Risk 7/5 and 4/3 subsystems. #701 now carries the Core-only Publish Readiness proof within the prior cumulative budget; the exact pre-split UI work is preserved at feature/vx-publish-readiness-v3-adoption-wip. VX-PUBLISH-READINESS remains non-PROVEN in this wave. Inheritance Intelligence and Visual Diff Intelligence remain PROVEN and lifecycle-closed. Smart Intent and Smart Auto-Fix remain blocked. Template #3 remains forbidden. Plan scope explicitly includes release-infrastructure because the task itself declares a release-budgeted split; this is intent scope only and does not weaken or alter the measured Release Risk Budget.
